newsitem.title: USA: U.S. merger boom led by telecoms, utilities in quarter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. merger boom led by telecoms, utilities in quarter.

text.p: The booming U.S. market for mergers and acquisitions ploughed ahead in the third quarter, led by deals in the telecommunications and utilities sectors and renewed activity in commercial banking, according to statistics released Tuesday.

More than $152 billion worth of domestic transactions were announced in the third quarter, making it the third-best period recorded by Securities Data Co., a Newark, N.J.-based company that tracks merger activity.
So far in 1996, U.S. firms have announced nearly $439 billion in deals, compared with a record-breaking $458 billion set in all of 1995, according to the data.

The pace was led by the telecommunications industry, which announced 70 deals valued at nearly $20 billion in the third quarter. Transactions included WorldCom Inc.'s $13.3 billion offer for MFS Communications Co. Inc.

It marked the second consecutive quarter that the boom was led by telecommunications, which has been invigorated by the Telecommunications Act of 1996, which aims to break down barriers to corporate unions.

The quarterly report issued by Securites Data ranked utilities as the third quarter's second-place leader, with 34 deals valued at about $15 billion. The sector's biggest deal of the quarter was Enron Corp.'s $3.2 billion bid for Portland General Corp.

Mergers in the banking sector, which slowed in the first six months of 1996 from last year's frenetic pace, picked up steam again in the third quarter. The industry generated $12 billion worth of transactions, led by NationsBank Corp.'s proposed $9.4 billion purchase of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc.
Securities Data said Morgan Stanley was the leading financial adviser for worldwide merger business in the first nine months of the year, completing 128 deals valued at more than $152 billion.
Among legal advisers, Skadden Arps Slate Meagher & Flom held the top post so far this year, with 71 deals valued at more than $125 billion.
